title: Preliminary Idea of Reaction Mechanism
notes: **Reaction mechanism:** step-by-step description of how a reaction occurs, showing bond breaking, bond making, and intermediate formation.
**Homolytic fission:** covalent bond breaks symmetrically, each atom gets one electron. Produces free radicals (species with unpaired electron). Occurs with non-polar bonds under heat or light.

**Heterolytic fission:** covalent bond breaks asymmetrically, one atom gets both electrons. Produces carbocations (electron deficient, positively charged) or carbanions (electron rich, negatively charged). Occurs with polar bonds in polar solvents.
**Electrophile:** electron-seeking species (electron deficient). Attacks electron-rich centres. Examples: $H^+$, $NO_2^+$, $Br^+$, carbocations.
**Nucleophile:** nucleus-seeking species (electron rich). Attacks electron-deficient centres. Examples: $OH^-$, $CN^-$, $NH_3$, $H_2O$.
**Free radicals:** neutral species with unpaired electron. Highly reactive, short-lived. Generated by UV light or heat. Example: $Cl\cdot$ in chlorination of methane.
